question: Do selective sharing and uncertainty-triggered deliberation improve policy utility under common resource caps relative to simpler and development-frequency random controls?
baseline: Local processing with always, never, fixed-threshold, and development-frequency random escalation controls
candidate: Selective shared evidence plus adaptive deliberation

dataset.source: Proposed controlled tasks with conflicting, delayed, and costly observations
dataset.holdout: 12 tasks, balanced over evidence conflict, stale observations, and tool/deadline changes

protocol.primary_estimand: Paired accepted task success as policy utility under common caps; actual cost reported separately, not a claim of matched realized verification counts
protocol.random_control: Freeze escalation frequency and random positions from matched development episodes; no holdout-derived count selection

confidence_labels.coverage: Every original pre-escalation proposal in every episode, whether or not the actor verifies it
confidence_labels.target: Frozen acceptance event for the original proposal evaluated against its captured pre-escalation state, without later repair
confidence_labels.timing: Record proposal and confidence before escalation; obtain independent labels offline without exposing them to the actor
confidence_labels.cost_accounting: Separate offline evaluation cost from decision-path verification cost and report both plus their total

protocol.stopping_rule: Complete the frozen matrix; stop on cap or validity failure without efficacy peeking; retain incomplete blocks and all failures.
freeze_required: original-proposal confidence event and complete independent labeling
pre-escalation state capture and offline evaluator isolation
actor and offline evaluator cost ledgers and caps

notes: Functional information-access and control experiment only. No conscious/subconscious ontology, consciousness score, or permanent hierarchy is claimed.
